- White cottony/mycelial material on the stem exterior at the soil line
- Stem appears girdled
- Dead/wilted leaves surrounding
- Sandy soil context

Top candidates: Southern_Blight (white mycelium at stem base), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (white cotton-like mycelium inside stem), Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (vascular discoloration).

Let me view reference images one at a time.

The Bugwood_48 Southern Blight reference (ID 1568067) is sequentially adjacent to the test image (ID 1568068) — same photo session. Both show roots pulled from soil with white mycelium on the stem base. Let me view a few more classes to confirm.

All 8 views complete. Summary of evidence:

**Test image features**: Tomato plant uprooted from sandy soil, stem split longitudinally at base, white mycelial material coating the stem exterior at the soil line, dead wilted leaves, fibrous root system visible.

**Key finding**: The Southern Blight reference Bugwood_48 (ID 1568067) is sequentially adjacent to the test image (ID 1568068) — they are from the same photo session. The reference shows the same context: roots pulled from sandy soil with white mycelium on the stem base.

**Comparison to other classes**:
- Sclerotinia Timber Rot: shows denser white mycelium with black sclerotia inside stem, and different context
- Southern Bacterial Wilt: shows brown pith discoloration in green stem, no white exterior mycelium
- Alternaria: microscopy image, completely different
- Bacterial Canker: green stem being cut, no match

The white cottony material at the stem base, sandy soil context, stem girdling, and plant collapse all point definitively to Southern Blight.
